ai.literal: A celestial maiden? Or a beautiful peacock? Or a woman wearing heavy earrings? Bewildered is my heart.
ai.translation: Is she a celestial maiden? Or a beautiful peacock? Or a mortal woman wearing heavy earrings? My heart is utterly bewildered.
ai.modern: இவள் ஒரு தெய்வப் பெண்ணா? அல்லது அழகான மயிலா? அல்லது கனமான காதணிகளை அணிந்த மனிதப் பெண்ணா? என்று என் நெஞ்சம் மயங்குகிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the protagonist's awe and confusion upon first seeing the heroine. Her extraordinary beauty makes him wonder if she is a divine being (அணங்கு), a graceful peacock (ஆய்மயில்), or a mortal woman adorned with heavy earrings (கனங்குழை மாதர்). The repeated use of the particle of doubt 'கொல்' and 'கொல்லோ' highlights his hesitation and inability to decide. Ultimately, his heart is left in a state of complete bewilderment ('மாலும் என் நெஞ்சு') by her mesmerizing presence.

ai.literal: She looked; looking in return to [her] look has [the quality] like a striking celestial maiden bringing an army.
ai.translation: She looked at me; and her looking back in response to my gaze was like a tormenting celestial maiden attacking with an army.
ai.modern: அவள் என்னைப் பார்த்தாள்; அந்தப் பார்வைக்கு எதிராக அவள் திரும்பப் பார்த்த பார்வை, ஒரு வருத்தும் தெய்வம் தன் படையைக் கொண்டு வந்து தாக்குவதைப் போன்ற தன்மையைக் கொண்டுள்ளது.
ai.explanation: The hero describes the overwhelming power of the heroine's gaze. When she returns his look, it is not a gentle glance but a force that completely conquers him. He compares her reciprocal look to a celestial maiden (அணங்கு) who attacks (தாக்கு) with the support of an army (தானை). The imagery of an army highlights how her eyes wage a beautiful but devastating war on his heart.

ai.literal: In the past I did not know that which is called the God of Death; now I have known [it]: with feminine grace, possessing large, battling eyes.
ai.translation: In the past, I did not know what the God of Death was. Now I know: it is a woman of great grace, possessing large, battling eyes.
ai.modern: முன்பெல்லாம் எமன் என்று சொல்லப்படுவதை நான் அறியாமல் இருந்தேன்; பெண் தன்மையோடு, பெரிய போரிடும் கண்களைக் கொண்டவளாக இருக்கும் இவளைக் கண்ட பிறகு இப்போதுதான் அதை அறிந்து கொண்டேன்.
ai.explanation: The hero is completely captivated and overwhelmed by the beauty and the piercing gaze of the heroine. He compares her gaze to the God of Death (கூற்று), who takes away a person's life. In the past, he only knew of Death as an abstract concept, but now he realizes that Death actually takes the form of a woman with feminine grace (பெண்டகை) and large, intense, battling eyes (பேரமர்க் கட்டு) that strike his heart.

ai.literal: Of those who look, the life-consuming by their appearance, of this womanly-natured simple girl, have become warlike, the eyes.
ai.translation: The eyes of this simple, feminine maiden have become warlike; by their very appearance, they seem to consume the lives of those who look at them.
ai.modern: பெண்மையின் மென்மை கொண்ட இந்த இளம்பெண்ணின் கண்கள் பகைமை கொண்டு போர் தொடுப்பவை போல உள்ளன; அவை தம்மைப் பார்ப்பவர்களின் உயிரைக் குடிக்கும் தோற்றத்தைக் கொண்டுள்ளன.
ai.explanation: The hero is captivated by the intense gaze of the heroine. Although she is a simple, innocent maiden (பேதை) endowed with gentle womanly qualities (பெண்டகை), her eyes (கண்) appear warlike and hostile (அமர்த்தன). By their mere appearance (தோற்றத்தால்), they have the lethal power to consume (உண்ணும்) the very life (உயிர்) of anyone who looks at her (கண்டார்). The couplet beautifully contrasts her gentle nature with the overwhelming, almost fatal power of her beauty.

words.gloss: Is it the god of death?

ai.literal: Is it the god of death? Is it an eye? Is it a female deer? The glance of this young woman possesses all these three.
ai.translation: Is it the god of death, or a beautiful eye, or a startled doe? The glance of this young woman possesses the qualities of all three.
ai.modern: இவள் எமனோ, கண்ணோ, பெண் மானோ? இந்த இளம்பெண்ணின் பார்வை இந்த மூன்று தன்மைகளையும் கொண்டிருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker is captivated and overwhelmed by the powerful gaze of a young woman. He wonders if her glance is the god of death because it steals his soul, a human eye because of its beauty, or the gentle eye of a female deer because of its innocence. The word 'மடவரல்' denotes a young, gentle woman, and 'நோக்கம்' refers to her glance. By combining these three elements, the couplet highlights the complex, mesmerizing, and life-altering impact of the beloved's first look.

ai.literal: If her curved eyebrows, without bending, hide them, indeed this woman's eyes will not cause trembling grief.
ai.translation: If her curved eyebrows would screen her eyes without bending, then surely this woman's eyes would not inflict this trembling distress upon me.
ai.modern: வளைந்த புருவங்கள் கோணாமல் அவளுடைய கண்களை மறைத்துக் காக்குமானால், இவளுடைய கண்கள் எனக்கு நடுங்கும் துன்பத்தைச் செய்ய மாட்டா.
ai.explanation: The speaker is overwhelmed by the beauty of the woman's eyes, which cause him a trembling distress. He imagines her curved eyebrows as guards; if they do not bend or deviate from their protective duty and instead completely screen her eyes, those eyes would not be able to look at him and cause such grief. The word 'kōṭā' means 'not bending' or 'not deviating', suggesting that the eyebrows must stand firm to shield him from the power of her gaze. Thus, the couplet uses the imagery of eyebrows acting as a barrier to the painful yet captivating power of her eyes.

ai.literal: Like the eye-shield upon a rutting male elephant is the fine cloth upon the firm breasts of this beautiful woman.
ai.translation: The fine cloth covering the firm breasts of this beautiful woman is like the protective eye-shield draped over a fierce, rutting elephant.
ai.modern: மதங்கொண்ட ஆண் யானையின் மேல் அணியும் கண்மறைப்புத் துணி போன்றது, இந்தப் பெண்ணின் நிமிர்ந்த மார்பகங்களின் மேல் அணிந்துள்ள மெல்லிய ஆடை.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the hero compares the garment covering the heroine's breasts to the protective eye-shield (கட்படாம்) of a rutting elephant (கடாஅக் களிறு). A rutting elephant is wild and dangerously powerful; similarly, the beauty of the heroine's breasts is overwhelmingly intense and capable of causing sweet torment to the beholder. The fine cloth (துகில்) acts as a shield, partially veiling this immense power and protecting the onlooker from being completely overcome. The word 'படாஅ' describes her breasts as firm and unconquered, mirroring the untamed strength of the 'கடாஅ' (rutting) elephant.

ai.literal: To the bright-foreheaded one, oh, broke indeed, in the battlefield, even enemies will fear, my strength.
ai.translation: Alas! My strength and valour, which even the fiercest enemies on the battlefield would fear, has been completely shattered by this bright-foreheaded maiden.
ai.modern: போர்க்களத்தில் பகைவர்களும் அஞ்சுகின்ற என்னுடைய வலிமையானது, இந்த ஒளிபொருந்திய நெற்றியை உடையவளுக்கு முன்னால், ஐயோ! உடைந்துபோனதே!
ai.explanation: The hero laments the sudden loss of his legendary strength in the presence of the heroine. He is a mighty warrior whose valour (pīṭu) strikes terror even in his enemies (naṇṇārum) on the battlefield (ñāṭpiṉuḷ). Yet, confronted by the beauty of this woman with a bright forehead (oṇṇutaṟku), his strength has completely shattered (uṭaintatē). The exclamation 'ōo' emphasizes his astonishment and vulnerability at being defeated not by weapons, but by love.

ai.literal: A female deer's beautiful gentle look and modesty to her who possesses, ornament what is it, external things having brought?
ai.translation: What is the use of bringing and wearing external ornaments for her who already possesses modesty and a gentle gaze like that of a doe?
ai.modern: பெண் மானைப் போன்ற மென்மையான பார்வையும் நாணமும் உடைய அவளுக்கு, வெளியில் இருந்து பிற அணிகலன்களைக் கொண்டு வந்து அணிவிப்பதால் என்ன பயன்?
ai.explanation: The lover admires the natural beauty of his beloved and declares that she needs no artificial decoration. He highlights two of her innate qualities as her supreme ornaments: her gentle, innocent gaze ('maṭanōkku') which resembles that of a startled doe ('piṇai'), and her natural modesty ('nāṇum'). The word 'ētila' refers to external, foreign things, meaning artificial jewels. The poet argues that for a woman endowed with such natural grace and character, adding external ornaments is entirely redundant.

ai.literal: Except in those who drank, brewed liquor, like love, to those who see, causing joy, does not do.
ai.translation: Brewed liquor does not, like love, cause delight to those who merely look at it; it only intoxicates those who actually drink it.
ai.modern: காய்ச்சிய மதுவானது, காமத்தைப் போலத் தன்னை வெறும் கண்ணால் பார்த்தவர்களுக்கெல்லாம் மகிழ்ச்சியைத் தருவதில்லை; குடித்தவர்களுக்கு மட்டுமே அது மகிழ்ச்சியைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the intoxicating power of brewed liquor (அடுநறா) with that of love (காமம்). Liquor is limited because it can only bring pleasure and intoxication to those who physically consume it. Love, however, is far more powerful as it brings instant joy and intoxication to those who merely look upon their beloved. Through this comparison, the poet highlights how the sight of the beloved alone is enough to induce a state of blissful intoxication.
